title: Getting more from each token: how Copilot improves context handling and model routing
gist: Copilot's automatic mode combines live model health (availability, load, speed, error rate, cost) with task intent scored by a routing model. It filters to models that clear a quality bar, then picks the best fit. It routes only on the first turn and after the context is compacted, because switching mid-conversation breaks the cached prefix.
changes: Routing here listens to the load on the models as well as to the task. And it names the safe switch points precisely: session start and compaction, where no cache is lost.
caveats: Baselines for the savings are not stated and the pool is five unnamed models. Lower plans are being moved to automatic mode as the only choice, which makes routing a capacity tool as much as a quality one.

numbers.baseline: a fixed mid-tier model, baseline not fully stated

bears_on.note: Another large harness routing between models by default, at cache boundaries only.
The route depends on live load on each model, not only on the request.

retired_why: GitHub replaced this router in October with one that decides for every prompt, so its account of routing only at cache boundaries no longer describes the product.
